sections.heading: Everyday Places QR Codes Do Real Work
paragraphs: A restaurant prints one code on each table, and diners open the menu without downloading an app or typing a long URL. Small businesses put codes on packaging so customers can reorder or watch a tutorial, turning a static product into the start of an ongoing relationship.

Event organizers embed registration links in flyers and badges, letting attendees register, find a schedule or join a channel before the doors open. Real estate agents place codes on signboards that open a virtual tour or a details page, capturing interested buyers the moment they stand outside the property.

Fitness studios and food trucks rely on codes that open a payment page or a reservation form, replacing the awkward back-and-forth of a cashier shouting a handle. Each of these cases hinges on one property: the code lands exactly where the person already is.

Wi-Fi codes are especially popular in cafes and co-working spaces. Instead of typing a long obfuscated password, a guest scans a code on the counter and connects. Guests remember the experience as effortless, and staff stop repeating the same password several times a day.

sections.heading: Error Correction and Scannability
paragraphs: Correction levels trade density for robustness: higher levels survive partial obstruction and low print quality.
The generated code places a proper quiet zone, essential for reliable scanning.
Professional print will read it everywhere, at any size.

sections.heading: Scannability, Print Size and Placement
paragraphs: The distance between the scanner and the code should match the size you print it. A menu code read from twenty centimeters away can be small, while a code on a billboard or a storefront window needs to hold up from across a street. Printing too small for the reading distance is the most common reason real QR projects fail.

The quiet zone, the empty border around the modules, is not decorative. Scanners need that blank margin to find the finder patterns at the corners, and some camera apps reject codes that touch other graphics or text. The exported code includes the correct quiet zone so the printed result scans cleanly the first time.

Contrast matters as much as correction level. Dark modules on a light background scan dependably, while color-inverted or low-contrast codes strain phone cameras. For critical placements, testing the printed code with more than one phone before a full run catches contrast problems early.

sections.heading: Download PNG or SVG for Any Surface
paragraphs: PNG covers screens, flyers and social posts; SVG scales infinitely for large-format print and vector workflows.
The exporter respects the selected size and silent-zone margin.
Total control over where your code goes next.

PNG presents no catch for a small menu or business card: it renders at full sharpness at modest sizes and uploads instantly. SVG should be the choice for a poster, banner or vehicle wrap, where the same file has to print both small and huge without any loss of crispness in the module edges.
